Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected for every tested request, across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not assume large size or repeated follow-up implies priority.
- No successful assignments yet. Option A (“standard queue”) remains the only untested/likely candidate, but this is not confirmed.
- Request wording, sender department, region, size, and urgency cues have not yet revealed a reliable rule. Test A next, especially for cases similar to those where B/C failed.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected across tested regions and request types. Continue avoiding C unless new evidence appears.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Size, urgency, or repeated follow-up alone do not justify B; no further B outcomes are known.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is now confirmed valid for small south-region refunds: REQ-2411 through REQ-2414 all succeeded, across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services senders and varied wording.
- Option A was rejected for:
  - Small east invoice (REQ-2410)
  - Small north claims (REQ-2415, REQ-2416)
  - Small south shipment (REQ-2417)
  - Large east invoice (REQ-2418)
  - Small south claim (REQ-2419)
- Do not generalize A beyond small south refunds. Request type and region appear more predictive than sender or wording; size may matter but is not yet isolated.
- Operations announced upcoming procedure changes affecting shipment and refund requests. Treat current routing evidence for those types as potentially temporary; re-test after the change.
- No successful assignments are known for invoices, claims, or shipments. C remains a poor candidate; test B selectively for non-refund cases while avoiding assumptions based only on urgency or size.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected across tested regions and request types. Continue avoiding C unless new evidence appears.
- Option D is now confirmed valid for refunds:
  - Large north refund (REQ-2420)
  - Large south refund (REQ-2423)
  - Small north refund (REQ-2429)
  D was invalid for a large north shipment (REQ-2422). Its broader applicability is unknown.
- Option A is confirmed valid for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across varied senders and wording.
- A was rejected for:
  - Small east invoice (REQ-2410)
  - Small north claims (REQ-2415, REQ-2416)
  - Small south shipment (REQ-2417)
  - Large east invoice (REQ-2418)
  - Small south claim (REQ-2419)
  - Large south refunds (REQ-2424)
- Option B succeeded for a large north claim (REQ-2421), but was rejected for a small south claim (REQ-2425) and for large/small north and small east shipments (REQ-2426–REQ-2428). Do not infer that urgency, size, or repeated follow-up alone justifies B.
- No successful invoice or shipment assignments are known. Shipment evidence currently rejects A, B, and D; procedure changes affecting shipments are imminent, so re-test after implementation.
- Region and request type remain more predictive than sender or wording. Size may matter, but is not isolated.
- For refunds, D is currently the strongest candidate across tested north/south cases; A remains supported only for small south refunds. Avoid generalizing beyond observed combinations.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has no successful assignments and remains unconfirmed; avoid unless new evidence appears.
- Option D is strongly supported for refunds:
  - Large north/south and small north/east refunds accepted (REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2429, REQ-2432, REQ-2433, REQ-2436).
  - Its broader applicability remains unknown.
- Option A is supported for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414). It was also accepted for a large north shipment (REQ-2430), correcting the prior assumption that shipment evidence only rejected A, B, and D. Shipment rules may still change soon.
- Option B is supported for:
  - Large north claim (REQ-2421)
  - Small north claim (REQ-2435)
  - Large east invoice (REQ-2438)
  It was rejected for small east claim, large south claims, small south claim, and several north/east shipments. Do not infer that urgency, size, or follow-up wording alone justifies B.
- Shipment evidence is mixed and sparse: A succeeded for large north; D failed for small north; B failed for large/small north and small east. Re-test after the imminent procedure change.
- No other invoice successes are known; B is currently the only supported invoice option, based solely on large east evidence.
- Region and request type remain more predictive than sender or wording. Size may matter but is not isolated; recent claims show strong regional variation.
- For refunds, use D as the leading candidate across observed north/east and north/south combinations; retain A only for observed small south refunds. Avoid generalizing beyond tested combinations.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has no successful assignments; avoid unless new evidence appears.
- Refunds: D is strongly supported for large north/south and small north/east, plus large east (REQ-2443). Continue leading with D for observed north/east and north/south combinations. A remains supported only for observed small south refunds. A procedure change is imminent; re-test afterward.
- Claims: B is supported for large north (REQ-2421), small north (REQ-2435, REQ-2448), but rejected for large east (REQ-2440, REQ-2446), small east, large south, and small south. A is now rejected for small south and large south (REQ-2441–2442). Regional patterns are strong; urgency and follow-up wording are not reliable.
- Invoices: B is supported for large east (REQ-2438, REQ-2447) and small north (REQ-2444). It is rejected for small south (REQ-2449). B remains the only supported invoice option, but applicability varies by region and size.
- Shipments remain mixed and sparse: A succeeded for large north previously but was rejected for another large north (REQ-2445); D failed for small north; B failed for large/small north and small east. Re-test after the imminent procedure change.
- Region and request type are more predictive than sender or wording. Size may matter, but evidence is inconsistent and not isolated. Do not generalize from a single size/region combination.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has no successful assignments; avoid.
- Refunds: Recent evidence overturns earlier assumptions. D is rejected for large south (REQ-2450, REQ-2458), and A is rejected for small south (REQ-2451). D remains supported only for observed large north/south and small north/east, plus large east; however, south results now conflict, so do not generalize. Re-test after the imminent procedure change.
- Claims: B is supported for large/small north, but rejected for large east, small east, large south, and small south. A is rejected for small and large south. Regional patterns remain stronger than urgency, sender, or follow-up wording.
- Invoices: B is consistently supported for small north (REQ-2444, REQ-2453), small/large east (REQ-2454, REQ-2456), and large east. It remains the only supported invoice option, but applicability elsewhere is untested.
- Shipments remain sparse and mixed: A failed for small east (REQ-2457) and small south (REQ-2459), as well as a prior small north; A previously succeeded once for large north but failed another time. B failed for large/small north and small east. A procedure change takes effect soon; re-test afterward.
- Region and request type are most predictive. Size may matter but is not isolated reliably. Do not generalize from a single size/region result. Treat tickets by their explicit request type; procedural memos may refer to a different category than the ticket text.
